questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down repeatedly, but not held down continuously.

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal gradually when stopping.

questions.question: Fueling a bus while passengers are on board is:

options.text: Recommended, but only if the passengers are told about the refueling.
Recommended, but only if time is an issue.

questions.explanation: Do not fuel a bus while passengers are on board. Never fuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: If you must leave the roadway and drive on the shoulder in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle has stopped, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle has stopped, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop. Keep one set of wheels on the pavement if possible. Avoid hard braking on the shoulder at speeds above 20 mph. Then signal, check mirrors, and merge back into traffic.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when it first begins to rain because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: Fresh rain mixes with oil drippings on the road, creating a slippery mixture.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, you can tell the ABS is not working if:

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When starting the engine, dashboard lights should turn on and then off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the ABS system is not working properly.

questions.question: A disruptive passenger should be:

options.text: Removed from the bus as quickly as possible, regardless of location.
Discharged at the next bus stop.
Kept on the bus and taken to the police department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discharged at the next bus stop.
questions.explanation: A bus driver is responsible for passenger safety. Discharge a disruptive passenger at the next scheduled stop or in a safe, well-lit area where people are present.

questions.question: When inspecting the interior of a bus, make sure:

options.text: Every seat is easy to remove.

questions.explanation: Check that all signaling devices work properly, including bathroom emergency buzzers and other safety features.

questions.question: Within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road, you must:
questions.explanation: Place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you signal.

questions.question: When driving, your mirrors should:

options.text: Not be used, as they are distracting.
Not be used unless there is traffic.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly to stay aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: How can you avoid distracted driving?

options.text: By not having complex conversations with passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: By not having complex conversations with passengers.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for something), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid difficult conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: When checking tires before a trip, what should you look at?
questions.explanation: When checking tires before a trip, make sure the tire pressure is correct. It should not be too low or too high.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. If two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what mirrors should you use?
questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often while backing.

questions.question: In cool weather, when ice begins to melt, what happens to the road?

options.text: It is usually safe to drive.
The road becomes even more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes even more slippery.
questions.explanation: As the temperature rises and ice melts, water sits on top of the ice. This makes the road even more slippery. Always slow down and drive carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: If vehicles have trouble passing your truck on a multi-lane road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane if your truck is moving slowly. Let other vehicles pass you using the left lane.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, what will you be asked to do?

options.text: Explain what you are inspecting and why.
Estimate the weight of a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. Explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Before driving downhill, what should you do?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Before going downhill, shift into a lower gear. This prevents you from using your brakes too much.

questions.question: What should you NOT use your mirrors for?

options.text: To check how fast you are traveling.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check how fast you are traveling.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly, especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight maneuvers. Do not use mirrors to check your speed. Use your speedometer instead.
